sections.text: Yellow perch fishing continued to improve over the past week. Anglers found fish straight out from Stony Point in 23 feet of water. Perch rigs with minnows and feathers performed well. The dumping grounds east of Luna Pier were also productive, although angler effort in that direction was light. Very few walleye were caught.

Fishing for yellow perch was very slow and spotty. Boat anglers tried several different spots with little to no success. Walleye anglers jigged in the lower part of the Saginaw River, catching one or two walleye at best.

Fishing was very slow over the past week. Some anglers fished for yellow perch off Sebewaing, Fish Point, Quanicassee, and farther offshore out to the shipping channel. Perch fishing was slow. A few anglers trolled for walleye off Fish Point in the slot with nightcrawler harnesses and body baits but had no success. Shore fishing was slow at all locations.
A few anglers targeted steelhead off the breakwalls but had no success.

Good numbers of immature Chinook salmon and steelhead were caught in 80 to 130 feet of water. The top 50 feet of the water column yielded the best results using green and orange spoons. Pier anglers were unsuccessful when targeting steelhead with spawn.

Boat anglers targeting salmon experienced slower fishing, with the most productive depth around 80 feet of water. Most fish were caught on spoons. Overall fishing activity was slow, and pier anglers reported slow action for all species. No yellow perch catches were reported.

Yellow perch fishing slowed slightly, though anglers continued to catch good numbers of quality-sized fish. Fish were more scattered, but depths around 60 feet of water were productive. Boat anglers targeting salmon also had fair success, with the best results in 80 to 100 feet of water. Spoons produced nearly all salmon catches. Pier fishing was slow for all species.
A fair number of salmon remained in the system. Anglers caught fish upstream at the Berrien Springs Dam, while anglers in the lower river also reported catching a fair number of fish.
Anglers targeting salmon reported slow fishing. Anglers reported salmon in the system but fishing was very slow.
Panfish were active and plentiful across most lakes for anglers actively targeting them.
Panfish were plentiful on most local lakes. Northern pike were caught on the Marble Chain of Lakes.
Salmon were reported running through the Grand River.

Chinook salmon were caught in the Tawas River on spawn and various artificial baits. A few walleye were caught from the pier. Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and an occasional northern pike were caught in the Au Gres River and from shore in the Standish area. Out from the Pine River, anglers caught primarily throwback yellow perch. Overall, boat activity remained low.

No boat activity was observed over the past week. A few anglers cast for Atlantic salmon and coho salmon from the pier with no success. Anglers targeting yellow perch inside the harbor reported only a few small fish in the area.

Chinook salmon were caught near the 9th Street Dam on spawn, beads, and crankbaits. A few Chinook salmon moved in over the past week along with a few steelhead. Anglers targeting steelhead and Atlantic salmon had the best results while fishing with beads. Coho salmon were reluctant to bite, but anglers who were successful cast spinners in gold, orange, and green.

There was heavy fishing pressure over the past week. Anglers experienced slow fishing. A few anglers reported landing a Chinook salmon. Anglers floating or bottom-bouncing spawn or beads had the most success. Spoons and minnow-style crankbaits were effective as well.

Anglers casting spoons off the pier reported catching a few coho salmon. Blue and silver or orange and gold were popular color combinations. A few walleye were also caught off the pier using jigheads with paddletails or split-tail plastics. Anglers fishing in the river caught a few Atlantic salmon on spinners and smaller streamers in bright white or olive. A handful of Chinook salmon were caught on body baits or floating skein under a float. Anglers also caught a few steelhead over the past week using streamers, spinners, and spawn bags.

Anglers casting body baits such as J-13s, flicker shads, and Thundersticks caught a few Chinook salmon. Anglers using skein under a float caught a few coho salmon and Chinook salmon. A few steelhead were caught by anglers casting spoons and spinners.
Pier fishing was slow, with only a few steelhead reported. Smallmouth bass and rock bass were caught on lures and worms. No boat activity was reported.

Pier fishing was slow, but a few steelhead were reported. Boat anglers caught a few steelhead and salmon around Big Sable Point in 60 to 80 feet of water when fishing the top 40 feet of the water column with spoons.
Anglers fishing the piers reported slow fishing for smallmouth bass when using natural bait.
Anglers fishing the Bear River reported slow catches of salmon. Fishing with spawn or skein produced the best results. Using beads and flies resulted in an occasional trout.
No boat activity. Pier anglers caught Chinook salmon while drifting beads, spawn bags, and skein from the docks.

Anglers reported a few Chinook salmon still entering the Betsie River. Two-year-old Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead were caught off the south breakwall when weather permitted. Casting Cleos and drifting or floating spawn yielded the best results.
Pier anglers reported some activity when casting spoons off the North Pier in the evening hours, landing a few Chinook salmon.

Panfish fishing was great across all lakes in the chain, with multiple anglers catching limits of large bluegill both from shore and on open water. Northern pike fishing was also good during the fall.

Fishing for bass and panfish was good to fair. Multiple anglers reported good bass catches after sunrise, and a few anglers caught limits of legal-sized bluegill. Anglers targeting northern pike also reported catching a few fish.
Walleye were caught in the late evening out of Brower Park and Davis Bridge.
Fishing was very good from kayaks and shore, with multiple panfish and bass caught.

Salmon entered the Muskegon River and were caught from Croton Dam downstream to Muskegon Lake. Deep-diver minnow plugs in the lower Muskegon River served as the primary lure. Good numbers of salmon were also present in the South Branch of the Pere Marquette River in northern Newaygo County. Fall walleye fishing picked up on Newaygo County inland waters.

Water levels dropped, and Chinook salmon were present in the Pentwater, White, and North Branch of the White rivers, with a mix of dark and fresh fish. Anglers also reported catching lake-run brown trout and steelhead in the White River.
Salmon were present in East and West Grand Traverse bays, the Boardman River, and Mitchell Creek.
Salmon were caught in the Betsie and Platte rivers.

Windy conditions restricted angling efforts and access to fishable areas. Anglers reported fair fishing when casting for northern pike and smallmouth bass. Northern pike anglers reported doing well near vegetation and windblown points. Anglers targeting walleye reported fair fishing in the upper bay, with expectations that action will improve as water temperatures decrease. Anglers trolled harnesses and casting jig heads with live bait.

Boat anglers found success targeting coho salmon while trolling the bay, with a few splake mixed in. Anglers fishing the mouth of the Anna River did well with coho salmon and splake when casting spoons and using spawn.

The river continued to see low angling effort over the past week as inclement weather impeded fishing conditions. A few anglers targeted walleye, though these efforts reportedly yielded minimal success.

Angling effort from the Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay access sites was low. Strong winds and heavy rain showers significantly limited lake access throughout the week. Angler reports were sparse, but included catches of lake trout, coho salmon, and Chinook salmon in low numbers. These fish were caught by anglers trolling in depths ranging from 20 to 100 feet of water. Shore anglers fishing from Union Bay also experienced limited success landing coho salmon in low numbers.

The harbor saw low angling effort over the past week as weather significantly limited lake access. As conditions allowed, anglers reported mixed catches of brown trout, coho salmon, and lake trout in low numbers. Reports indicated that these fish were caught by anglers trolling in 20 to 120 feet of water. Shore anglers reported no success fishing from the breakwalls or within the harbor.

Few Chinook salmon were caught in the Carp River and offshore in Lake Huron near Nunns Creek. Anglers floating or bottom-bouncing skein had the most success. Salmon were also caught on spoons, beads, spinners, and minnow-style crankbaits.
Anglers fishing the mouth of the Sucker River caught coho salmon and a few rainbow trout while casting spoons and using spawn.

Chinook salmon were reported in the river, with anglers catching them on beads, skein, and shallow-diving, brightly colored crankbaits or spinners. Anglers reported that fish appeared to be nearing the end of the run, though enough fish remained in the river to provide active angling.

No creel interviews were conducted with any boat anglers targeting lake trout. A few reports indicated shore anglers caught lake trout and coho salmon off the lower breakwall near the lighthouse during early morning and late evening hours. Boat anglers trolling near the river mouths out of Lower Harbor caught fair numbers of coho salmon and steelhead, along with an occasional Chinook salmon. Brown trout remained one of the most consistently caught species in both the Chocolay River and Carp River. Following recent rain, fish movement upstream increased significantly, resulting in a substantial surge in coho salmon numbers. Anglers also reported catching steelhead in the Carp River, with a few additional reports from the Chocolay River, particularly near the river mouth.

No targeted lake trout effort was observed over the past week, though anglers caught a few incidentally while trolling for other species in Au Train Bay in shallow depths of 20 to 45 feet of water. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in shallower water reported marking high densities of fish on electronics and experiencing fair success when weather permitted. Boat anglers reported high fish counts on sonar in front of river mouths and near Scott Falls.

Anglers reported fair fishing, with catches consisting primarily of coho salmon and splake while trolling and casting near shore around river mouths. A few brown trout were also caught. Shore anglers reported steady fishing over the past week, with many catching coho salmon and splake. Anglers jigging for lake trout and lake whitefish reported a slow bite.

Inclement weather and wind reduced angling pressure in these ports. However, anglers who were able to make it out reported fair fishing for lake trout while trolling spoons and flasher-and-fly combinations in 80 to 120 feet of water. Anglers also reported a few coho salmon in low numbers.

Fishing pressure in the area slowed significantly due to windy and rainy weather. No angling activity was reported in DeTour. In Hessel, pier anglers caught an occasional northern pike. Anglers also caught a few yellow perch out of the Cedarville boat launch and around the Government Bay area.

Yellow perch anglers experienced a slight resurgence over the past week. Anglers fishing east of Sterling State Park toward the Ohio state line in 24 feet of water caught decent-sized yellow perch on minnows. Multiple limits were not reported for multi-person boats. Water temperatures continued to drop, helping improve activity. A few walleye were caught in the same area on nightcrawler harnesses, though catches were scattered. Smallmouth bass fishing on Lake Erie was good using various artificial lures.
Fishing pressure was low over the past week. A few yellow perch were caught east of the Spark Plug in 20 feet of water, with morning hours being most productive.

When weather permitted, boat anglers caught immature Chinook salmon and steelhead in 50 to110 feet of water. Orange and green spoons fished in the top 50 feet of water worked best. Anglers casting from the breakwalls were unsuccessful targeting mature Chinook salmon.

Decent numbers of immature Chinook salmon and steelhead were caught in 60 to 150 feet of water. Orange, green, and yellow spoons worked best when targeting the top 60 feet of water. Pier anglers targeting Chinook salmon were unsuccessful.

Boat anglers caught good numbers of fish. Anglers targeted fish in approximately 100 feet of water. Pier fishing slowed, though an occasional salmon was still caught. Casting spoons was the most productive method. Overall fishing was very slow, and no yellow perch were reported.

Boat anglers caught a few fish, with the most productive water located around 80 feet of water. Fishing was slow overall, but that remained the most effective depth. Pier fishing was very slow for all species. Yellow perch fishing continued to produce good results. Fish remained scattered, with 40 to 60 feet of water proving to be the most productive range.
Decent numbers of salmon were caught in the lower river as well as at the Berrien Springs dam.
Coho salmon and Chinook salmon were caught in the Tawas River. A few yellow perch were caught off Standish. Otherwise, fishing effort was light.

Very little boat activity was observed over the past week. Anglers who targeted deeper water reported catching lake trout, steelhead, Atlantic salmon, and an occasional walleye. Standard-sized spoons trolled in 30 to 50 feet of water yielded inconsistent success. No fishing activity was reported on the pier.

Anglers reported a slow bite. Spinners, small crankbaits, and drifted beads yielded some success for coho salmon and Atlantic salmon. Chinook salmon turned dark, but anglers continued to catch fish on spoons and spawn. A few steelhead were taken on drifted beads and small spawn bags.
Boat anglers reported a few steelhead and immature Chinook salmon while trolling in 40 to 80 feet of water. With cold water temperatures, the best results came in the top 25 feet of the water column.

There was a mixture of silver and dark Chinook salmon at the Cheboygan Dam spillway. Anglers who floated or bottom-bounced spawn were the most successful, landing up to three salmon. Spoons and minnow-style crankbaits were productive as well.

Anglers targeting salmon off the pier experienced a slow week, with a few Chinook salmon and coho salmon caught. Glow spoons and body baits such as bandits, flicker shads, and Rapala J-13s were popular choices. Anglers targeting channel catfish off the pier with nightcrawlers and cut bait had decent success.

Anglers casting Rapala J-13s, flicker shads, and Jr. ThunderSticks in black/silver and fire tiger colors caught a few Chinook salmon. Glow spoons and skein were also successful. A few steelhead and coho salmon were caught on spinners.

Pier fishing was slow. Anglers fishing straight out and south caught a limited number of Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in 150 to 200 feet of water at various depths. Fish were caught from 20 to over 100 feet down on plugs and spoons.

Anglers fishing the Bear River reported slow fishing for Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead. Anglers had success using spawn and skein in the Bobber Hole early in the morning. Those casting from piers reported occasional bites using spoons.

Anglers launching at the Center Road boat launch caught a few cisco along with a few Chinook salmon when trolling in 110 to 140 feet of water. Anglers who had success trolled a mix of spoons and plugs roughly 60 to 80 feet down. A few smallmouth bass were also caught along the breaks in 25 to 45 feet of water.

Anglers targeted steelhead off the piers as water temperatures cooled, though action was slow. Coho salmon and Chinook salmon remained in the area as they slowly moved toward river mouths. The Betsie River continued to hold good numbers of Chinook salmon in deep holes and near Homestead Dam. Boat anglers caught a few Chinook salmon and coho salmon in front of the piers early in the morning on spoons. As morning conditions cleared, anglers moved out to the shelf to target steelhead in the top 30 feet of water.

Anglers targeting yellow perch reported scattered schools and had difficulty locating fish. Some anglers reported catching yellow perch in shallow water using worms. Walleye anglers reported slow fishing, though fishing overall was good. Drifting or trolling crawler harnesses worked well. Anglers also reported having success using jigheads tipped with nightcrawlers or leeches. Coho salmon anglers reported slow fishing and fewer fish sightings. Anglers fishing the Escanaba River had success.

Over the past week, the river experienced very light angling effort. Rough weather conditions throughout the week hindered fishing conditions on occasion. Catches of walleye were reported in very low numbers.

The Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay access sites all experienced light angling effort over the past week. Heavy winds and frequent rain showers limited lake access on multiple days. Anglers reported catches of lake trout, coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and brown trout in low to fair numbers. Fish were caught by anglers trolling in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet of water.

Angling effort from the harbor was light over the past week. Inclement weather limited lake access. When weather permitted, anglers reported mixed catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout in low numbers. These fish were caught by anglers trolling in depths of 30 to 150 feet of water.

Overcast conditions made for good fishing, with anglers catching fish throughout the day. Most anglers caught at least one fish, while a few others landed up to 10 fish. Floating or bottom-bouncing skein produced the best results. Salmon were actively moving in and out of Nunns Creek, while a fresh push at the Carp River provided anglers with an opportunity to hook into a silver Chinook salmon at the Carp River cement footing pier. Salmon were caught throughout the stretch between McDonald Rapids and the Carp River cement footing pier. Other productive bait options included spoons, minnow-style crankbaits, and spinners. Glow baits were effective before daybreak and after sunset.
Shore anglers caught coho salmon and rainbow trout at the mouth of the Sucker River. Fishing with spawn and casting spoons brought success. Boat anglers did well jigging for lake trout.

Anglers reported Chinook salmon and pink salmon in the river. Anglers reported having the most success using skein, though some anglers had success using spinners and shallow-diving crankbaits. Orange, chartreuse, and pink were popular lure colors. The best success occurred at night and early in the morning.

Anglers caught lake trout in 80 to 160 feet of water. Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks, as reports west of the Chocolay River yielded poor results. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, primarily near the bottom using downriggers. A few reports indicated anglers caught lake trout and coho salmon off the lower breakwall early in the morning and near sunset. Anglers trolling the river mouths near Lower Harbor caught decent numbers of coho salmon and Chinook salmon. Brown trout and coho salmon were caught in both the Chocolay River and Carp River. Fish numbers increased with cooler evening temperatures.

The tribal nets were removed, opening the Flats northwest of Au Train Island toward Five Mile Point for lake trout fishing. The Wood Island Reef and areas northwest of Au Train Island out toward the Laughing Whitefish River also remained available for lake trout fishing, while Au Train Bay to the Laughing Whitefish River was open for salmon, brown trout, and steelhead. Anglers jigging near Au Train Island in 40 to 80 feet of water had good success catching lean lake trout. All lake trout caught were near the bottom while trolling or jigging. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in 10 to 60 feet of water marked numerous fish.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing, with catches consisting primarily of coho salmon and splake while trolling near river mouths, along with a few brown trout. Shore anglers reported that the bite picked up, with many anglers successfully catching coho salmon and splake. Anglers jigging for lake trout and lake whitefish reported a slow bite.

Anglers reported fair fishing for lake trout when trolling spoons and flasher/fly rigs around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. Anglers reported a few coho salmon, but in very low numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers in Hessel caught a few yellow perch near the buoy straight out from the Cedarville boat launch. A few northern pike were caught off the pier in Hessel. Smallmouth bass anglers had good success fishing around island rock piles and points. Splake fishing was slow due to 66-degree water temperatures within the marina. Splake season is now closed. In DeTour, anglers caught good numbers of lake trout prior to the season closing. Lake trout season is now closed, and fishing pressure in DeTour was minimal.

I’m looking forward to some cooler temps, migratory fish, and all of the other activities that the fall season brings. We are capping off the summer season mousing… There’s still a week or two left…

Unfortunately the weather did not really cooperate and it made for a tough couple of days of fishing. Early in the week we had some cloudy weather which made for a good iso bite…

The flooding and worm flow events shuffled the deck and gorged the fish. I spent a significant amount of time searching water for rising fish…
